benchmarkEvidence.referenceLightingAnchor: Prior actual Store-reference inspection records premium toy-boutique language: warm key, gentle cool/pink fill, dimensional material response, clean silhouettes and physically grounded contact shadows. This file does not claim a new reference-pixel inspection.

tier3Minimum: Garment identity must be readable before theme decoration: hoodie/vest/smock construction cannot depend on color or motif alone.
A true three-quarter read must expose front plus a meaningful side/depth plane, not a frontal poster shape with rim lighting added afterward.
Fabric must show category-specific structure such as folds, baffles, ribbing, seams, pockets, armholes, ties or layered panels; at least one construction feature must create self-shadow/occlusion.
Theme marks must behave as material treatment or attached construction, not as a flat graphic pasted over a generic garment.
At Store-card scale the outer silhouette and one or two identity-defining construction cues must remain legible without relying on detail-view inspection.
tier4Minimum: Must visibly step above accepted Tier-3 Tops 7-9 in material richness or construction complexity, not merely in glow strength or ornament count.

Accepted Tops-10 benchmark combines padded panel volume, ribbed trim, zipper/sleeve hardware, material-specific specular response and controlled cyan/magenta reflected light while preserving bomber readability.
Padding/quilt recipes need local compression at seams and changing highlight width across curved baffles; evenly spaced flat bands are insufficient.
Hard hardware and soft textile surfaces must not share the same highlight model; zippers/pulls/snaps should read harder and sharper than cloth.
tier5Minimum: Tier-5 silhouette must advertise the step-up before fine detail: longer or more architected outerwear, layered construction and stronger depth hierarchy are expected.
Premium complexity should come from physically plausible layers, drape, quilting, closures, pockets and selective metal/acrylic details rather than uniform sparkle/noise.
At least three distinct depth zones should survive the detail render: foreground hardware/edge, primary garment shell, and recessed/overlapped inner layer or cavity.
Lighting may be richer than Tier 4 but cannot substitute for cloth thickness, fold tension, seam compression or garment length.

tops11RepairThresholdIfV7LaterFails.reviewFirstRule: The exact v7 asset must first be repository-staged/read back and rendered at card/detail scale. No verdict transfers from v5/v6.
boundedRepairThreshold: Preserve an unmistakable jacket body and attached sleeve volume; avoid a torso made of parallel graphic stripes.
Padded baffles should wrap around the torso/sleeve curvature with seam compression and changing light across each inflated section.
Show a recessed hood/collar cavity plus zipper and pocket hardware that clearly separates hard surfaces from padded textile.
Candy Core should come from confection-like pink/cream/lilac material accents integrated into panels/piping/hardware, not a candy-colored flat overlay.
At card scale the jacket must read as more materially sophisticated than accepted Tops-8 Puffer Vest while still clearly different from Tops-10 Star Bomber.

tops12RepairThresholdIfV7LaterFails.reviewFirstRule: The exact v7 asset must first be repository-staged/read back and rendered at card/detail scale. No verdict transfers from v5/v6.
boundedRepairThreshold: Coat length must be obvious at card scale; the silhouette should extend materially below a standard jacket hem and retain a coherent lower-body drape.
Three-quarter construction should expose overlapping storm/yoke or front-panel layers, side depth and a recessed inner opening rather than a flat symmetrical front.
Quilted or padded zones need loft plus seam compression while woven coat zones need softer fold tension; do not render every surface as the same smooth plastic.
Adventure Club identity should come from functional explorer-like details such as belt, pockets, compass-inspired hardware, reinforced panels or straps without copying third-party IP.
Tier-5 spectacle should be selective: premium metal highlights, layered materials and grounded shadow/reflection, while coat silhouette and construction remain the first read.

tier1Minimum: Even Starter headwear needs real wearable construction: band thickness, clip hardware, panel seams, brim curvature or visible fasteners as appropriate.
Theme-specific finish must be restrained enough that the item category remains the first read.
Paired/small accessories need separated silhouettes and hardware that survive card reduction.
tier2PlusMinimum: Tier progression should introduce deeper folds/volume, richer support construction or materially richer settings—not just a larger shape or brighter gradient.
Accepted Headwear-4 Berry Bow demonstrates deep satin folds, stitched edges, wrapped center, visible band support and a jewel accent while remaining readable at card scale.
Future crowns/ears/halo pieces must show how they physically attach to the wearer: bands, clips, supports, prongs, seams or brackets cannot be implied away.

exactHashReviewChecklist: Confirm repository-stored bytes and exact candidate hash; local/external-only receipts are not reviewable.
Inspect actual shared card and detail pixels for that exact hash; no source-only approval.
Judge identity before theme decoration, then silhouette/depth, material response, construction/hardware, tier progression, card readability, originality and near-duplicate risk.
Compare Tier-4/5 candidates against accepted lower-tier benchmarks so higher tier is visually richer for construction/material reasons rather than glow alone.
Do not transfer any REWORK/BLOCKED verdict to a new hash; record a new independent decision from the new pixels.
Every qualified ACCEPT is handed to 08 immediately; reviewer 01 never canonical-wires.
